primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent quantitative elliptic source estimate with one fixed scalar admissible tester, full matrix coefficients, exact quadratic weight conjugation and an actual Banach-controlled H2 graph.

source_correspondence: E0 states the complete uniform matrix, compact full-kernel, elliptic and whole-input product-cone hypotheses. The output is the actual ordinary H2 graph with one fixed scalar admissible source test.
E1 retains the exact imaginary first-order term in x-squared P and proves a uniform matrix normal-cap inverse bound on one collar independent of the target order.
E2 differentiates the inverse in the actual matrix order and proves every uniform principal and complete-symbol inverse estimate.

E3 constructs the full target parametrix by ordered corrections and compact-parameter Borel summation, including every lacunary, cutoff and proper-support residual. Actual input projections stay inside the permitted patch.
E4 moves the quadratic boundary weight through the entire ratio kernel, with the correct t-squared multiplier and every side-face and residual term.
E5 proves all mixed derivatives through order two as actual boundary source tests. The shifted normal factors retain their lower constants and no normal derivative of the forcing is required.
E6 applies the exact Banach distribution bound and finite residual source tree to the full parametrix remainder. No boundary residual is called an ordinary smooth kernel.

E7 places every derivative test and residual child into one bounded full-kernel family satisfying the whole-input cone hypothesis. The existing exact Fourier factorization supplies one scalar tester independent of the coefficient parameter.
E8 proves injection of the tested graph completion into B using flat transposed tests, identifies the actual output and source limits, and retains both true traces and zero-Dirichlet closure.
E9 gives the sharper L2-only source order and distinguishes this elliptic component from characteristic and global propagation. Its geometric neighborhood is fixed before the finite target order.
The three complete solutions check all shifted normal factors, exact scalar normal-cap separation and an actual noncommuting two-by-two inverse in both multiplication orders.
Twenty-eight exact checks and 228 rendered formulas support the analytic review.
